newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets seen lifted by U.S., Japan outflows.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets seen lifted by U.S., Japan outflows.

text.p: Asian markets will reap the benefit of outflow of funds from developed markets in 1997, Jardine Fleming Securities said on Thursday.

"Emerging markets have lagged their developed counterparts in Europe and the United States for almost three years now, but the historically low valuations of Asia's markets should prove to be the catalyst sparking a resurgence of funds flows from developed to developing markets," Jardine Fleming's regional strategist, Colin Bradbury, said in a news release.
Asian markets will benefit from renewed weakness in Japanese stocks as well as expectations that the U.S. equity market will fail to repeat its strength of last year, Jardine Fleming said.
But the performance of Asian markets will continue to vary widely and careful selection will remain necessary, it added.

Jardine Fleming warned against aggressive profit-taking in strong markets such as Hong Kong and the Philippines, which it expects to continue enjoying superior performance while some of the poor performers continue to lag.
Hong Kong is gaining on the elimination of its discount ahead of the transfer of sovereignty to China on July 1, while economic reforms are boosting shares in the Philippine market, it said.
"As interest rates continue to fall and earnings growth remains the strongest in the region, the (Philippine) market is set to repeat its strong 1996 performance," Jardine Fleming said.

Thailand and South Korea will continue to perform poorly, it said. Thailand is not yet close to resolving serious structural problems, while South Korean stocks are facing similar long-term concerns, it said.
Laggards Singapore and India should see an improvement in their prospects in 1997, Jardine Fleming added.

Singapore is heading for a steady economic recovery over the course of the year, while Indian valuations have adequately discounted the political and economic problems that depressed stocks last year.
